newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end sharply lower on bonds, dollar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end sharply lower on bonds, dollar.

text.p: French stocks slumped on Monday, mirroring falls in the dollar and bond prices on worries that U.S. interest rates are headed higher, brokers said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 57.24 points, or 2.16 percent, at 2,588.38, while the CAC-40 March futures contract fell 39 points to 2,601. The bourse's drop gathered pace after a drop in Wall Street share prices in early trading.
Volume was 5.9 billion francs, relatively low compared with recent sessions, with many investors sidelined ahead of U.S. housing starts on Tuesday and inflation data on Wednesday.
Several traders expect the CAC index to continue its consolidation to around 2,550 points before setting a new trend.

Financials were weaker, with Assurances Generales de France shares easing 3.61 percent to 200.50 francs. The share has been pressured by signals it may be seeking an acquisition after the Axa-UAP megamerger.
Shares in tyremaker Michelin rose against the trend, closing up 1.07 percent at 339.60 francs, ahead of the 1996 results due early on Tuesday.
Analysts expect a profit jump despite charges to restructure its Spanish operations and cut 1,445 jobs in France.

A consensus estimate of more than 40 brokers compiled by consultants Jacques Chahine Finance shows a median forecast of 3.4 billion francs of net attributable profit for 1996, up from 2.8 billion for 1995.

Shares in electronics firm Compagnie des Signaux jumped 4.71 percent to 309 francs on a report in the Tribune newspaper that said the Lagardere Group was keen to get Cie des Signaux to participate in a bid for Thomson-CSF.
